questions.q: What probability and forecast category does Cascade's Equipment Proposal stage use?
options: 10% / Pipeline
50% / Best Case
75% / Best Case
100% / Closed
questions.explain: The stage table sets Equipment Proposal at 50% probability with a Best Case forecast category, between Needs Analysis (25%) and Negotiation/Review (75%).

questions.q: Why are Closed Won and Closed Lost each configured as "Closed" stages, and what does that configuration unlock?
options: It unlocks a discount on the Opportunity's Amount field
It lets reports correctly exclude them from open pipeline forecasts, and it's the trigger Chapter 3's record-triggered Flow watches for
It automatically deletes the Opportunity after 30 days
It prevents the Opportunity from ever being reopened for any reason
questions.explain: The lesson states marking these as Closed stages matters for both reporting (excluding them from open pipeline) and automation (Closed Won is the exact trigger the Chapter 3 Flow watches for to create an Installation Project).

questions.q: What does the Loss Reason field capture, and when does Chapter 3 enforce it as required?
options: Why a deal didn't close; a Chapter 3 validation rule requires it only when Stage = Closed Lost
Why a deal closed early; it's required on every Opportunity at creation
The competing vendor's name; it's required when Stage = Qualifying
The installer assigned; it's required when Stage = Closed Won
questions.explain: The lesson creates Loss_Reason__c as a picklist and notes a Chapter 3 validation rule will require it only when Stage is set to Closed Lost.

questions.q: Why does an Opportunity at Cascade need Products attached rather than just an Amount field?
options: Salesforce does not allow a currency field on Opportunity
Products are required to change the Opportunity's owner
It's what makes a deal an actual equipment package, tied to the Opportunity Product object from the Lesson 3 data model
Amount fields are deprecated in current Salesforce releases
questions.explain: The lesson states that attaching Products via Add Products is what makes a deal an actual 'equipment package' instead of a single number, directly fulfilling the Opportunity Product relationship designed in Lesson 3.

questions.q: In the walked-through example, what does Tom Baptiste do right after the site visit, and what stage does the Opportunity move to?
options: He sets Stage to Closed Won immediately after the visit
He adds products (the range and the hood) and moves the Opportunity to Needs Analysis
He marks the deal Closed Lost due to no budget
He reassigns the Opportunity to Priya Nair
questions.explain: The walkthrough describes Tom adding the range and hood products after the site visit and then moving the Opportunity to the Needs Analysis stage.
